newsitem.title: UK: Argentina says Falklands still mar ties with UK.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says Falklands still mar ties with UK.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Secretary Guido Di Tella said on Thursday that ties between his country and Britain had improved signifcantly but they were no nearer to resolving their differences over the disputed Falkland Islands.
"If we want a solution, we can have a solution but we have to meet around the table," he told journalists after meeting his British counterpart Malcolm Rifkind.

He acknowledged that the British election on May 1 would clear the table and might allow the two countries to continue discusssions more fruitfully, but said it did not matter which party won because their position on the islands was the same.
"If the government has a clear majority then I think we have the political basis for advancing discussions and reaching an agreement," he said.

But Di Tella conceded that nothing could be decided unless it is the wish of the 2,000 residents of the remote islands in the South Atlantic. Britain has consistently said it refuses to share or transfer sovereignty of the territory.
Argentina and Britain fought a 10-week war over the islands in 1982. Although Argentina lost, it maintains its claim to the sparsely-populated archipelago, which it calls the Malvinas.

The two countries have since restored diplomatic relations and in 1995 signed a deal to explore for oil in waters around the Falklands, but fishing rights and sovereignty of the islands have been stumbling blocks in closer ties.
